questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Honestly it was a bit random, but I chose Prague because it is a beautiful city with a deep cultural history, and a very nice contemporary art scene! It also helped that Charles University has a lot of courses available for international students

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was very accessible !

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: some online meetings, one registration day, but otherwise you were kind of on your own when it came to reaching out and finding out more information if needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was totally fine, but at my faculty (Faculty of Arts) there wasn't really any orientation program so you kind of had to find people to mix with on your own.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I posted in different housing groups on facebook, and got quite a lot of offers through that. The hard part was going through them all, and sorting out the scammers. I recommend looking in the facebook group called "AVU ♥", where a lot of younger people post about renting out their apartments. Otherwise the classic "apartments in prague..." groups are fine too! Paying much over 15.000 czk a month for a room is considered expensive by locals, but there is a housing crisis in prague so it could be tricky to find something much cheaper as an outsider (from my experience).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would totally recommend it. The people I met that lived in the dorms were not so happy with the condition (or location), but they got a nice community there which is something you don't really experience if you're living alone!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the registration process itself was easy enough, but there were so many courses to look into which was quite confusing and time consuming - and the course catalogue changed a lot from the arrival to the actual registration period.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: registration opened at around 7 or 8 if i remember correctly, so you had to be ready at your computer to sign up for your preferred courses, especially if they had a low capacity. The add-drop period was about a month, so you had a lot of time to try out different courses and then see if you liked them and wanted to continue!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you can always contact the erasmus office, they are very nice

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not successful since most of them were cancelled/not available to me anyways... but found some nice courses that made up for it

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: register for as many courses as you want in the add/drop period and try out a lot of different stuff!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was all very chill, I think coming as an erasmus student the teachers don't have the highest expectations. But the level differs a lot, some courses just consisted in watching films and then saying if you liked them or not, while others had some heavier reading. But all in all, it was very chill.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Totally different. Every course has max 6 ECTS, so you never really get that deep into a topic which i think differs a lot from my experience at KU (and you have to take way more courses which i found a bit tricky to balance). There was mandatory attendance in all of my courses which also was new to me, and the exams were totally different from what i was used to from back home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

ADU100809	(M)othering in Contemporary Art
AFSV00458	Pictures and Images. Philosophical Reflections

ASEV00565	Hungarian Cinema (Summer Semester 2025/26)
ASV00022	Dressing up Oneself and the Society: Fashion in the 19th and 20th Century Aesthetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Pictures and Images. Philosophical Reflections was great, and the teacher was very engaging! 
Slovenian cinema after 1990 was my favorite one, but just consisted of us watching film from slovenia, so it was maybe not so academic in the classical sense, but very fun and interesting and i learned a lot about slovenia!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected cost, but you can definitely live for much cheaper! I was eating out almost every day and drinking a lot of coffee and beer :)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries more expensive, coffee way less expensive! The cinema is also very cheap (Bio oko, Lucerna etc.)!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there was a broad variety of sport courses available, but i really didn't look too much into it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: didn't really look into it

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out and explore, have fun! Enjoy being in a beautiful and cheap city! Please go outside of the city center! The Stromovka park has become my favorite park in the whole world. Klub AVU is a very nice place to go for beer, it is the cafe belonging to the Art Academy but open for everyone!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Prague, go for hikes, the nature is beautiful!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, people are a bit shy and reserved in public, but almost everyone (young and old) was super friendly and helpfull once you approached them! As long as you respect your elders, and are not too obnoxious in public, people will really show you a lot of respect. Although people can be quiet they are also very straight forward and say what is on their mind, which is something to get used to... and their humour can also be a bit extreme and confusing and a bit vulgar, so don't get too shocked!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A lot of the classes i had were almost exclusively erasmus students. But go up to the local students and ask for tips, ask if they want to do group projects together, invite them for a beer! Everyone is most likely very interested in getting to know you and to hear about where you come from.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People working service jobs are not always the friendliest, which is something I was not used to at all, but I can really appreciate - they don't care much if you don't like them, they aren't putting up a facade, and they are not pressing for tips - so don't take it personally! Getting used to the drinking culture was also a bit of an adjustment - people often drink one or two beers quite early in the day and that's it. Most people also drink and go out during the weekdays and then use the weekend to relax and sober up haha

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is great (although a bit challenging as a vegetarian, but hey still great), the beer is amazing and cheap (the more foam the better), the people are super nice and fun, and there is a lot going on in the cultural life - a lot of nice museums, cinemas, theaters, and there is just so much to learn about Czech culture and Prague's history.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't put too much pressure on the academic experience
2. walk as much as you can! Although the public transport is great (and cheap), Prague is a very walkable city, and you discover so many things by walking 
3. Go with the flow, things can be stressful, but all the paperwork and all the practical stuff will sort itself out!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: nothing comes to mind

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the city. truly such a nice and safe city to live in.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: managing my own expectations when it came to my courses. surrendering to the fact that the teachers don't expect much from me, and that i don't have to stress about not being stressed or challenged.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
